notes: Invoice INV-1005 and receipt REC-1005 both cite PO-1005, but no purchase order document was provided for this case, so the PO referenced cannot be verified as existing or matching. Amounts (59000.0 INR) are consistent across invoice, bank statement, ledger entry, and receipt, and the bank statement/ledger both reference INV-1005, supporting a coherent payment trail. However, REC-1005 is dated 2026-07-18, three days before the invoice date of 2026-07-21, which is an unusual sequence (receipt predating invoice) that internal consistency of amounts cannot resolve or excuse. Tax amount is not separately broken out on the ledger entry or receipt (both note GST is bundled/inclusive), so tax reconciliation relies solely on the invoice's stated tax_amount of 9000.0 and cannot be independently corroborated. The bank statement confirms a successful settlement matching the invoice amount, but this alone does not verify that any payment-terms condition (e.g., receipt-before-payment) was actually satisfied - only the receipt document, whose date is anomalous here, can speak to that, and its early date undermines rather than confirms fulfillment of such a condition.
